body: A key that suddenly stops working with your ignition puts you in an immediate bind. Whether you are dealing with a lost key, a stolen one, or a cylinder that has simply worn out, you have two main paths forward: an ignition rekey or a full ignition replacement. Knowing which option fits your situation saves time and money. Our techs at Be Secure Locksmith can walk you through both. This post breaks down how each service works, what conditions call for one over the other, and what you can expect from the process.

An ignition rekey changes the internal pin configuration inside your ignition cylinder so that a new key operates it. The cylinder itself stays in place. A tech removes it, adjusts the wafers or pins inside, and reinstalls it so your vehicle responds to a freshly cut key. This process works well when the cylinder is still in good physical condition but the key has been lost, stolen, or compromised. If you recently bought a used vehicle in the Ocala area and want to make sure old keys no longer work, a rekey is a cost-effective way to restore control over who can start your car. Our ignition repair service covers both rekeying and cylinder-related work, handled on-site at your location.

An ignition replacement involves removing the existing cylinder and installing a new one. This is the right call when the cylinder itself has worn down, become damaged, or failed mechanically. Signs that point toward replacement include:

• A key that turns but does not fully engage the starter
  • A cylinder that feels loose or sticky even with a working key
  • Visible damage from a break-in attempt
  • Consistent failure after years of heavy use

No amount of rekeying will fix a component that is past its useful life. Our automotive locksmith services in Ocala include full ignition cylinder replacement with on-site service, so you do not need to arrange a tow to a shop.
Which Option Is Right for Your Situation?

The condition of your current cylinder is the deciding factor. If the cylinder turns smoothly and only the key itself is the problem, a rekey is typically the more affordable route and gets the job done without replacing functional parts. If the cylinder grinds, wobbles, or fails to engage consistently, replacement is the more reliable long-term fix. A tech can assess the cylinder on the spot and tell you which path makes sense before any work begins. One Ocala customer reached out after his Honda Accord ignition stopped responding to his key. JJ arrived on-site, assessed the cylinder, rebuilt the ignition lock, and cut two new working keys without requiring a shop visit.
Does a Rekeyed or Replaced Ignition Need New Keys?

Yes, in both cases you will need a new key cut to match the updated or replaced cylinder. If your vehicle uses a transponder key or a smart key with an embedded chip, that key also needs to be programmed to your car's system. Our techs handle the full process, including cutting and programming, at your location. This is especially relevant for newer vehicles common throughout Ocala and Marion County, where most keys carry electronic components. For a closer look at how key programming works across different vehicle types, the car key programming page covers what is involved for domestic and foreign vehicles alike.
What About Cost Differences Between Rekeying and Replacing?

A rekey is generally less expensive than a full replacement because it uses the existing cylinder and involves less labor. Replacement costs more because it requires sourcing a compatible new cylinder and completing a more involved installation. That said, paying for a replacement when one is actually needed is still typically more affordable than a dealership service visit, and the work gets done at your location. You can find general price ranges on our locksmith service price list, and our team is happy to provide a specific estimate based on your vehicle's make, model, and year before scheduling anything.
Choosing the Right Service in Ocala, FL
Both ignition rekey and ignition replacement are practical solutions depending on what is actually wrong with your vehicle. Here is a quick summary to help you decide:

• Choose a rekey if the cylinder works fine but the key has been lost, stolen, or needs to be changed
  • Choose a replacement if the cylinder grinds, wobbles, or fails to start the vehicle reliably
  • Ask for an on-site assessment if you are unsure which issue applies
